text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context:
An institutional records office maintains permanent student files containing enrollment data, grade records, degree conferral certificates, and credential verification responses. Standard filing practice stores original documents in physical or electronic repositories, indexed by student ID and program. Retention policies typically preserve records indefinitely for completed degrees, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Auditing mechanisms include audit logs tracking who accessed records and when, plus reconciliation between internal gradebooks and issued credentials. Verification services (e.g., National Student Clearinghouse) cross-check claimed credentials against institutional databases using unique identifiers like degree type, date, and institution code.
2) What occurred:
The actor produced a document resembling an official transcript and a separate diploma-style document, both containing a named account holder, a program title, a date of completion, a grade sequence, and an institutional seal. The transcript field population followed a standard academic format with course listings, credit hours, and cumulative GPA. The diploma document included an authority signature block and an embossed or printed seal. Both documents were transmitted to an employer via a named channel. The actor subsequently provided the employer with instructions to present these documents to a registrar verification contact and a background screening service, using a dated record format matching the fabricated completion date.
3) Materials/access observed:
Observed materials included: (a) a transcript document with course-level entries, (b) a diploma document with conferral language, (c) a seal or logo element matching the target institution's branding, (d) a named account reference, (e) a specific completion date, (f) a transmission channel record showing document delivery, and (g) a verification-request correspondence referencing the documents by filename and date.
4) Indicators & artifacts:
Detection indicators include: mismatch between degree dates and enrollment period in any legitimate record; absence of the named account in institutional student information systems; verification request returning "no record found" despite provided documentation; metadata showing document creation timestamps post-dating the claimed completion date; seal or logo quality inconsistent with official institution artifacts; and correspondence channels showing direct document transfer to verification parties rather than institutional issuance. Artifact signatures: PDF metadata with non-institutional creation tools, image-based seal placement, and font choices not matching institutional templates.
